title: Same event sent twice by two setups
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: Each platform gets one hit per action: one page_view / PageView per page load and one add_to_cart / AddToCart per Add to Cart click, and gtag.js loads once per Measurement ID.
fails: A platform app, the store's built-in integration, GTM and a hard-coded snippet each send the same pixel or GA4 event, so the network log shows two or more hits for one action (often two gtag loads or two GA4 configs for one ID).
validate: Browser: on home, product and cart (phone and desktop), count gtag/js loads per Measurement ID and collect hits per event name per platform (google-analytics collect, facebook.com/tr, analytics.tiktok.com, tr.snapchat.com, googleadservices) for one page load and for our one Add to Cart click; list each pixel/measurement ID and where it loads from (app script, GTM, inline HTML in the crawl).
action: Send the network capture to the developer and ask them to keep one setup per platform (app or GTM, not both) and remove the extra snippet.
done_when: The network log shows exactly one hit per platform per page load and per Add to Cart click.
why_it_matters: Double events inflate reported conversions and feed the algorithm a false signal, so reported ROAS reads higher than real and audiences fill with wrong people.
selected_because: Tested failing in real stores (gtag double-load 3 of 5, duplicate pixel sources 2 of 3) and fully visible in the network log; the GA4 and GTM copies of this check were merged here.

title: Our Add to Cart click really fills the cart
group_en: Paid clicks reach the cart
group_ar: الزيارات المدفوعة بتوصل للسلة
pass: On the worker's phone visit, our one click on the product page's Add to Cart puts the item in the cart: a cart drawer with the item opens, or the store's cart count goes above zero, and the cart page lists it.
fails: The button is not clickable, or after the click the drawer is empty, the cart count stays at zero and the cart page is empty.
validate: Browser facts from the worker's own store visit (src/fud/collect.ts addToCartAndCapture, reported by src/site-checks.ts as addToCart): it selects variants, clicks Add to Cart once, waits for a drawer or a URL change, reads the store's cart count, then opens the cart page. Pass when addToCart.ok is true with via=click. Fail on reason atc_not_clickable, atc_drawer_empty or an empty cart page. When the click left the cart empty but the store's own cart endpoint filled it (via=api), report 'unconfirmed, may be our automated browser', not a broken button. A disabled button (atc_disabled_or_out_of_stock) is reported under sold-out products, not here. Attach the cart crop screenshot.
action: Send the screenshot and the step that failed to the developer to fix the Add to Cart button or the theme script behind it.
done_when: A re-scan shows addToCart.ok via the click: the item reaches the drawer or the cart page on a phone.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks that cannot add to cart cannot buy, so CVR drops and CAC rises on the same spend.
selected_because: The biggest post-click leak we can prove with our own click; moved here from the Conversion list and sourced on the worker's own add-to-cart visit, not on the cart-icon checklist item.

title: Pixel missing or blocked for a platform you run
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: Meta, TikTok, Snap and Google Ads tags all load and send hits (not blocked) on the paid path.
fails: A platform has no pixel, or the pixel script loads but its hits fail or are blocked (CSP, script error), so that platform never sees visits or sales.
validate: Crawl HTML for pixel IDs plus browser network requests to each vendor on home, product and cart; record loaded, fired, blocked or failed per platform. Which platforms carry spend is not visible to us, so list every platform found and every one missing for the buyer to match against their accounts.
action: Tell the store owner which platform has no working pixel; the developer adds it through GTM or the platform app.
done_when: Each platform you advertise on shows its pixel hits in the network log on home, product and cart.
why_it_matters: A platform with no pixel cannot see sales, so reported ROAS reads low and its algorithm optimises blind.
selected_because: Without a working pixel no other tracking point matters for that platform; Snap and TikTok coverage is often missed.

title: Click IDs and UTMs lost between the ad click and the cart
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: A landing URL with utm_* plus fbclid, ttclid, ScCid and gclid reaches the final page in one hop with every parameter intact; the first GA4 hit carries the UTMs in page_location; _fbc, _ttp, the Snap click cookie and _gcl_aw are set; and the Meta, TikTok and Snap hits on the product page and after our Add to Cart click still carry the click IDs.
fails: A redirect (http to https, www, trailing slash, language or country switch, link shortener) drops the query string, nothing stores a click ID, or it is gone by the cart, so the sale is credited to direct or not matched to the ad.
validate: Browser (phone): open home and one product URL with test utm_source/medium/campaign and test fbclid, ttclid, ScCid and gclid; record the redirect chain and final URL, page_location in the first GA4 collect hit, the _fbc / _ttp / Snap / _gcl_aw cookies, and the fbc, ttclid and ScCid values on pixel hits on the product page and after our Add to Cart click. Gateway redirects after the cart are not checked.
action: Ask the developer to keep the full query string on every redirect (language, country, www, https) and let each pixel store its click ID on the first page.
done_when: Every test parameter survives to the final URL in one hop, the cookies hold the test click IDs, and the Add to Cart hits carry them.
why_it_matters: Lost click IDs and UTMs push paid sales into direct and stop the platforms tying the sale to the click, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and winning campaigns can get cut.
selected_because: One live test for every click ID and UTM, merged from the copies that sat in all four lists; the browser is the tool that measures it.

title: Tracking missing on pages your ads land on
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: GTM (with the same container ID as the one we read) and the pixels load on home, collection, product, cart and GA4's top paid landing pages.
fails: A template (often collection, cart or a landing page built outside the theme) has no tag, or the site loads a different container ID from the one the team edits, so visits there are not counted.
validate: Crawl and browser: GTM snippet and container ID in the HTML and a gtm.js request on home, one collection, one product, the cart and GA4's top campaign landing URLs; pixel requests per page; compare the container ID with the one read via the service account.
action: Ask the developer to install the store's GTM container on every page template, including landing pages built outside the theme.
done_when: Every checked page loads the same container ID, it is the one the team edits, and the pixels fire there.
why_it_matters: Pages with no tracking send no events, so sales from those landing pages go uncounted and reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: Tested in audits (3 of 5 stores failed placement); the GTM list's crawl copy of this check was merged here.

title: Live product and cart events sent without value, currency or items
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: view_item and add_to_cart (and the matching ViewContent / AddToCart pixel hits) carry value, currency and items[] / content_ids.
fails: The dataLayer or pixel hit has no value, no currency, or an empty items array, so the platform gets the event but not what it was worth.
validate: Browser: read the dataLayer ecommerce objects and the GA4 and pixel hit parameters for view_item and our add_to_cart on the product page; flag missing value, currency or items. Purchase is not observed because the visit stops at the cart.
action: Ask the developer to add value, currency and items to every ecommerce push and map them in each pixel tag.
done_when: Every ecommerce event on product and cart shows value, currency and items in the dataLayer and in each platform's hit.
why_it_matters: Events without value starve value-based bidding and catalogue retargeting, so reported ROAS reads low and the algorithm optimises on counts, not money.
selected_because: Value and currency gaps failed in 3 of 5 tested stores; this reads the live hits, while the Purchase mapping is read from the container.

title: Consent state on live hits blocks or ignores ad tags
group_en: Consent and data the platforms may reject
group_ar: الـ consent والداتا اللي المنصات ممكن ترفضها
pass: With no banner choice, the gcs/gcd consent state and the pixel hits match the store's region policy; after accept, all four Consent Mode v2 signals (ad_storage, analytics_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization) turn granted and ad tags fire; after refuse, marketing tags stop.
fails: The default denies everything so visitors who never touch the banner send no ad hits, only the two older consent signals are sent, or the banner choice changes nothing on the hits.
validate: Browser: record gcs/gcd on Google hits and which vendor hits fire before any choice, after accept and after refuse (separate visits). If no banner shows, record the default state only. This point reads live hits only.
action: Ask the developer to connect the banner to Consent Mode v2 with all four signals and check the default state for GCC and Egypt visitors.
done_when: Before a choice the hits match the region policy, after accept all four signals show granted and ad tags fire, and after refuse no marketing tag fires.
why_it_matters: Over-blocking hides real sales from the platforms, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and Google's modelling has less to work with.
selected_because: Consent blocking ad tags is a named under-count cause; the live Consent Mode v2 check from the GTM list was merged here, the container default stays in GTM.

title: Our successful Add to Cart reaches GA4 and every pixel
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: After our click fills the cart, the dataLayer gets an add_to_cart push and GA4 and each pixel found on the page record an add-to-cart hit.
fails: The item lands in the cart (often from a drawer or quick add) but GA4 or a pixel records no add-to-cart event.
validate: Browser facts: atcEvents from the worker's visit (dataLayer entries, GA4 event names and vendor:event pixel hits recorded after the click, src/fud/collect.ts eventsAfterClick), read only when addToCart.ok is true; compare with the pixels found on the page.
action: Ask the developer to send add_to_cart on every successful add, including the drawer and quick add.
done_when: After a successful add, GA4 and every pixel on the page record one add-to-cart event.
why_it_matters: Missing Add to Cart events thin the mid-funnel signal and retargeting audiences the algorithm uses.
selected_because: Spec scores Add to Cart signal medium-high; checked with our own click. The trigger setup that can fire on non-adds is read in the container.

title: Value sent as text or in the wrong currency
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: value is a plain number equal to the shown price, and currency is a three-letter ISO code that matches the price the shopper sees.
fails: value arrives as a string with a symbol or a comma decimal (so it is cut or misread), or currency is lowercase, a symbol, or a different currency from the page.
validate: Browser: compare the dataLayer and pixel value/currency for view_item and add_to_cart with the price and currency shown on the product page and in the cart; flag type, format or currency mismatch.
action: Ask the developer to send value as a number and currency as the ISO code of the price shown.
done_when: value equals the shown price as a number and currency matches the page on product and cart.
why_it_matters: A wrong value or currency makes every reported sale worth the wrong amount, so reported ROAS can read high or low and value bidding learns from bad numbers.
selected_because: Distinct from presence: this checks correctness of the number the platforms optimise on.

title: Product IDs differ between pixels, GA4 and the page
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: The product ID in Meta content_ids, TikTok content_id, Snap item_ids, GA4 item_id and the page's product schema SKU/ID is the same value.
fails: A pixel sends a variant ID, handle or SKU while the other sources use a different ID, or IDs are scraped from page text and break on some products, so catalogue ads cannot match the viewer to the product.
validate: Browser: on the product page and after our Add to Cart click, compare content_ids / content_id / item_ids in pixel hits with GA4 item_id and the JSON-LD sku/productID. The catalogue feed itself is not readable; mark 'confirm the feed uses the same ID'.
action: Ask the developer to send one product ID, from the dataLayer, to every platform, matching the catalogue feed.
done_when: All four platforms and the schema show the same product ID on the checked product.
why_it_matters: Mismatched IDs quietly break dynamic product ads and catalogue retargeting, so those campaigns learn from fewer matches.
selected_because: High-impact (I4) catalogue-ad failure; the GTM list's copy of the same live comparison was merged here.

title: Main content shows late after the ad click
group_en: Speed after the ad click
group_ar: السرعة بعد الضغط على الإعلان
pass: LCP under 2.5s on the product and home page on a throttled phone.
fails: LCP over 2.5s, so paid visitors wait for the main image or headline.
validate: Browser: performance trace with mobile throttling on home and product (LCP, plus TTFB and the LCP element).
action: Ask the developer to preload the hero/product image and cut render-blocking files.
done_when: LCP under 2.5s on a phone on home and product.
why_it_matters: People who leave before the page shows never become a landing page view, so the click-to-LPV gap widens and CAC rises; ad-side LPV is not visible to us.
selected_because: Speed after the click is in the section scope; slow paid landings failed in 3 of 4 tested stores.

title: Script errors stop tracking and the cart
group_en: Paid clicks reach the cart
group_ar: الزيارات المدفوعة بتوصل للسلة
pass: No JavaScript errors on product and cart that stop later dataLayer pushes or the cart from working.
fails: An error (often repeating) breaks the cart script or stops the pushes that follow it, so later events never fire.
validate: Browser: console errors on home, product and cart, matched to the dataLayer pushes and hits that follow them.
action: Send the console log to the developer to fix the erroring script.
done_when: No console errors on product and cart, and all expected events still fire.
why_it_matters: Errors cut both conversions and the events that report them, so CVR drops and reported ROAS reads low.
selected_because: One error can break both buying and counting; fully checkable in the console.

title: Pixel fires too late in the page load
group_en: Speed after the ad click
group_ar: السرعة بعد الضغط على الإعلان
pass: The Meta PageView and the other pixels send their first hit early in the load, not after heavy scripts or a late GTM trigger.
fails: Pixels wait for window load or a delayed GTM trigger, so visitors who leave early are never counted.
validate: Browser: on home and product (throttled phone), record the time of each platform's first hit against first paint and load; read the GTM trigger type for the base pixel tags where the container is readable.
action: Ask the developer to fire base pixels on page initialisation instead of window load.
done_when: Each platform's first hit is sent before the page finishes loading on a throttled phone.
why_it_matters: Late pixels miss early leavers, so landing page views and visits are under-counted and the click-to-LPV gap looks worse than the page alone.
selected_because: Explains part of the link-click to LPV gap, which buyers see daily but cannot diagnose.

title: Non-standard event names
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: Ecommerce events use the standard names (view_item_list, view_item, add_to_cart; ViewContent, AddToCart).
fails: Custom names (for example productView, addtocart) that the platforms do not map to standard events.
validate: Browser: list event names in the dataLayer and in pixel/GA4 hits on collection, product and cart; flag non-standard names.
action: Ask the developer to rename events to the platforms' standard names.
done_when: All ecommerce events seen use standard names.
why_it_matters: Custom names are not used for standard optimisation or reports, so the algorithm gets a thinner funnel signal.
selected_because: Failed in 3 of 5 tested stores; directly limits what platforms can optimise on.

title: Personal data in page URLs
group_en: Consent and data the platforms may reject
group_ar: الـ consent والداتا اللي المنصات ممكن ترفضها
pass: No emails or phone numbers in query strings sent with pixel or GA4 hits.
fails: A form or login puts email or phone in the URL, which the pixels then pass on.
validate: Browser and crawl: scan visited URLs and the dl / page URL parameters of pixel and GA4 hits for email or phone patterns.
action: Ask the developer to send forms by POST and strip personal data from URLs.
done_when: No email or phone appears in any URL or hit parameter on the visited pages.
why_it_matters: Platforms can flag or restrict events that carry personal data in URLs, which cuts the signal campaigns optimise on; check warnings in Events Manager.
selected_because: Real link to ads: platforms can restrict events with personal data in URLs.

title: Taps lag on the phone after the ad click
group_en: Speed after the ad click
group_ar: السرعة بعد الضغط على الإعلان
pass: No main-thread task over 200 ms while home and product load on a throttled phone.
fails: Long script tasks block the page, so taps on variants and Add to Cart lag or are missed.
validate: Browser: performance trace with mobile throttling on home and product; list main-thread tasks over 200 ms and the scripts behind them.
action: Ask the developer to split or defer the long scripts named in the trace.
done_when: No task over 200 ms on load on home and product.
why_it_matters: Paid visitors who tap and get no response leave or give up on the add, so CVR drops on clicks already paid for.
selected_because: Backfill: current-tool check of tap delay on the pages paid traffic lands on.

title: dataLayer set before the tag loads
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: The page declares dataLayer and pushes page and product data before the GTM snippet, so the first events carry that data.
fails: dataLayer is declared after the container, or product data is pushed late, so page_view and view_item fire before the data exists or the data is overwritten.
validate: Crawl and browser: position of the dataLayer declaration and first pushes against the GTM snippet in the HTML of home and product, and the order of dataLayer entries against the first GA4 and pixel hits.
action: Ask the developer to declare dataLayer and push page data above the GTM snippet.
done_when: On home and product, dataLayer and the page data come before the GTM snippet and the first hits carry the data.
why_it_matters: Events that fire before their data reach the platforms with empty values or items, so value bidding and catalogue ads get less to learn from.
selected_because: Backfill: tested in CRO audits (1 of 2 failed); the order is readable in the page source and the dataLayer.

title: Heavy or blocking files on first load
group_en: Speed after the ad click
group_ar: السرعة بعد الضغط على الإعلان
pass: No render-blocking CSS/JS in the head, JS + CSS on first load under about 1 MB, text compressed, static files cached long, no autoplay hero video on the phone first screen, and text visible while Arabic fonts load.
fails: Blocking or oversized files delay first paint, text is sent uncompressed or static files are cached briefly, a hero video fills the phone first screen, or text stays invisible until the font loads.
validate: Browser (phone): performance trace (render-blocking resources), JS and CSS transfer size, response encoding and cache headers, first-screen media, and font-display on home and product.
action: Ask the developer to defer non-critical scripts, trim unused code, turn on compression and caching, replace the phone hero video with an image, and show text while fonts load.
done_when: No render-blocking files, first-load JS + CSS under about 1 MB, compressed and cached files, no phone hero video, and text visible during font load.
why_it_matters: Heavy first loads slow the page after the click, so more paid visitors leave before the landing page view and you pay for clicks that never saw the store.
selected_because: Main fixable cause behind slow paid landings; the Conversion list's speed point (hero video, compression, caching, fonts) was merged here.

title: Failed or hanging requests on landing pages
group_en: Speed after the ad click
group_ar: السرعة بعد الضغط على الإعلان
pass: No 404/500 requests and no request over 3 seconds blocking content on home, product or cart.
fails: Images or scripts fail, or a slow request holds back what the shopper sees.
validate: Browser: network log status codes and durations on home, product and cart.
action: Ask the developer to fix or remove the failing and slow requests.
done_when: No 404/500 and no blocking request over 3 seconds on those pages.
why_it_matters: Broken or stalled pages lose paid visitors before they act, so CVR drops on the same clicks.
selected_because: Post-click leak visible in the network log.

title: Third-party apps slow the page
group_en: Speed after the ad click
group_ar: السرعة بعد الضغط على الإعلان
pass: Chat, review and popup apps load light or after the main content.
fails: Third-party app scripts make up most of the load weight.
validate: Browser: transfer size and timing by third-party domain on home and product.
action: Ask the store owner to remove unused apps and the developer to load the rest after the main content.
done_when: Third-party apps no longer dominate load weight on home and product.
why_it_matters: App weight slows the page after the ad click, so CVR drops and the click-to-LPV gap widens.
selected_because: Common speed leak on app-heavy stores; measured per domain.

title: Page jumps while it loads
group_en: Speed after the ad click
group_ar: السرعة بعد الضغط على الإعلان
pass: CLS under 0.1 on home and product on a phone.
fails: Content shifts as images, banners or apps load, so shoppers tap the wrong thing or lose their place.
validate: Browser: CLS and the shifting elements from the phone performance trace on home and product.
action: Ask the developer to reserve space for images, banners and app widgets so the page doesn't shift.
done_when: CLS under 0.1 on home and product on a phone.
why_it_matters: A page that jumps under the thumb causes mis-taps and drop-offs right after the click, so CVR is lower than the traffic deserves.
selected_because: Backfill: current-tool Core Web Vitals check not yet covered by the speed points.

title: Embedded widgets that hide conversions
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: Any iframe that takes an action on the visited pages (form, booking, embedded checkout) passes its events to the parent page's dataLayer.
fails: The action happens inside an iframe, so GA4 and the pixels on the page never see it.
validate: Browser: list iframes on home, product and cart and their domains; where one is a form or checkout, check for postMessage pushes into the parent dataLayer. Checkout after the cart is not checked.
action: Ask the developer to relay iframe events to the page's dataLayer.
done_when: Actions inside the iframe show as dataLayer events on the parent page.
why_it_matters: Conversions inside iframes never reach the platforms, so reported ROAS reads low for campaigns that drive them.
selected_because: High-impact (I4) under-count cause; iframe presence on visited pages is checkable.

title: Old cart items attached to new events
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: ecommerce is set to null before each new ecommerce push.
fails: No clearing, so items from an earlier push merge into the next event.
validate: Browser: dataLayer sequence on product then cart; check for ecommerce:null before each push and for items carried over.
action: Ask the developer to clear the ecommerce object before each push.
done_when: Each ecommerce push follows an ecommerce:null and carries only its own items.
why_it_matters: Carried-over items inflate item counts and values on later events, so product-level numbers read higher than real.
selected_because: Over-count source visible in the dataLayer sequence.

title: Item fields use old or platform names
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: items[] use item_id, item_name, item_brand, item_category, item_variant, price, quantity.
fails: Legacy or platform-native field names (id, name, product_id) that GA4 drops, leaving item reports as (not set).
validate: Browser: read item field names in dataLayer ecommerce objects on product and cart.
action: Ask the developer to map the platform's item output to the GA4 item fields in GTM.
done_when: All items show the standard field names in the dataLayer.
why_it_matters: Dropped item data blanks product reports and the audiences built from them, which weakens product-level signal.
selected_because: Common platform quirk; readable directly in the dataLayer.

title: Product schema price or stock wrong
group_en: Shopping and catalogue signals
group_ar: إشارات الـ Shopping والكتالوج
pass: Product pages carry Product + Offer schema whose price and availability equal what the page shows.
fails: Schema missing price or availability, or showing a different price or stock than the page.
validate: Crawl: JSON-LD Product/Offer on the product page vs the visible price and stock.
action: Ask the developer to make the schema use the live price and stock.
done_when: Schema price and stock match the visible page.
why_it_matters: Google Shopping can disapprove products whose page data disagrees, which cuts Shopping and Performance Max reach.
selected_because: Real link to Google Shopping ads approval.
